subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should the Slack plugin own native OAuth token rotation, and where should Slack client secrets, refresh tokens, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and adopted at runtime?
rationale: This changes credential persistence, OAuth secret custody, and live Slack auth behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the secret storage, redaction, migration, recovery, and operator UX model.

options.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
options.body: Build rotation inside the Slack plugin with secure storage, transactional refresh, status/doctor recovery, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.

options.title: Create a generic refresh seam first
options.body: Define a reusable credential-refresh contract before implementing Slack as one consumer if maintainers want token refresh to generalize beyond Slack.

options.title: Defer to external rotation
options.body: Keep OpenClaw on static Slack token inputs for now and document external rotation or manual operational workarounds until maintainers want to own rotating Slack secrets.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned rotation
recommendation.body: Build rotation inside the Slack plugin with secure storage, transactional refresh, status/doctor recovery, docs, and live Socket Mode plus HTTP Mode proof.
